verdict.rationale: Ardent ships a documented first-party CLI with dedicated reference pages for overview, auth, configuration and branches. It has agent-friendly features: stable JSON output and JSON errors with codes, `--print-url`, token-based auth with no login step, and idempotent re-runs. Its docs explicitly describe coding agents running the CLI themselves and an ardent-cli skill. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the CLI's behavior, since the community evidence doesn't discuss the CLI.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: ardent branch info my-feature --format json # prints a stable JSON object
Set ARDENT_TOKEN and run commands normally — no login step
Errors are JSON too, with a stable `code`
The agent runs the Ardent CLI itself — creating, using, and deleting its own branches
With the ardent-cli skill installed, a short ask is enough — the skill fetches the current docs and works through setup
